scope: The main application keeps the graph-theoretic asymptotic and the finite Lindemann-Weierstrass input as explicit hypotheses. Passing does not prove those two external theorems. OrderedCancellation verifies the abstract filtered ring and finite-packet recursion only; it does not formalize tournament kernel costs, permanent recovery, or Condition R. ColorEnergy verifies finite prefix-energy algebra only. ColorTransport proves actual word reachability and an area lower bound. ColorTransportExact proves attained minimum distance and color-word energy repair paths. ColorGraphRepair supplies matrix energy and actual finite differing-edge bounds for normalized color-word tournaments, extended by ColorCutNormalization to arbitrary color words. ColorTargetModels supplies independent carousel/doubling isomorphisms. DiamondFreeRepresentation constructs a color-word representation from the actual zero diamond count; ZeroDiamondRepair exports original-tournament finite differing-edge bounds to independent carousel/doubling targets for D=0. Positive-diamond repair and Condition R remain outside this result. DiamondGap proves only finite tournament diamond coverage and D=0 or n<=4D; this does not imply Condition R. VectorWeakMajorization verifies finite Abel, square-sum comparison and a signed matrix bound. The cone/sign/selection modules prove K cone/prefix preservation and the combinatorial envelope<=P_k, and SelectedTournamentMajorization completes actual finite tournament vector weak majorization, independently checked from raw matrix entries. ReferenceMomentComparison supplies the concrete K-square conjugacy and all nonnegative-integer-power Frobenius comparisons. Negative/fractional powers, small-defect sixth-order identities and Condition R are not proved. ReferenceOnesOrbit identifies the actual all-ones orbit; TournamentEnergyRowDomain proves source-energy series convergence and comparison for q>=0 with q*(n-1)^2<1, including q=1/n^2 for n>0 without a Summable premise. TournamentSourceResolvent proves the actual source resolvent identity, both inverse identities, and comparison on that same real nonnegative row domain. No enlarged complex domain or full R is asserted. OrdinalSixthPolynomial proves only explicit polynomial subtraction and conditional scalar transfer, with the actual ordinal-matrix sixth-moment identification now supplied by OrdinalSixthMatrixBridge for arbitrary finite skew block families. TournamentSourceEnergy identifies directed cycle counts/3 with the source deficit, and OrdinalGlobalSixthDeficit proves the actual global-transitive-reference sixth deficit formula. The small-block bound retains explicit size and D-versus-triangle assumptions; DiamondTriangleIncidence proves D<=(n-3)t for actual unordered counts, and SmallDiamondComponentReduction proves actual source-switched SCC size bounds for positive small D. Complete ordered SCC matrix reconstruction and the final unconditional sixth-deficit bound/R remain outside scope. ActualPathConvolution proves exact S1 even-subset convolution for this repository hamiltonianPathCount, with no convolution assumption; DiamondFreePathAverage proves the exact normalized two-permanent average for the original hamiltonianPathCount under the actual zero diamond count, without principal-minor or convolution assumptions; no asymptotic recovery or R is implied.
